newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian woman, hit by poverty, wants to rent womb.
newsitem.headline: Indian woman, hit by poverty, wants to rent womb.

text.p: Nirmala Devi says she wants to rent out her womb to pay for medical care for her paralysed husband.

The 30-year-old in the Punjab state capital told Reuters on Wednesday: "My husband has been bedridden for over five years. I have been working as a domestic helper. I also have to bring up our small son. We are heavily in debt."

She said a childless couple had offered her 50,000 rupees ($1,396) to bear a child for them. "I have taken my husband into confidence about the proposal. We need money and the couple want a child," Devi said.

Nirmala Devi, her husband and their five-year-old son moved to Chandigarh about four months ago from a Punjab village after selling their small piece of land because they could no longer make both ends meet.
India has no laws governing surrogate parenthood, and so Nirmala Devi has filed an application before a local judge asking that her action be declared legal.
"I do not want to be harassed and humiliated by society and I want the child to be legitimate," she said.
Her lawyer Navjit Singh Brar said he was confident the judge would give Devi a favourable ruling.
"She is a bold woman and she is pursuing a noble cause. She is a devoted wife and wants her husband to get proper medical treatment," Brar said.

He said he has separately moved an application before the same judge asking that Devi not be prosecuted by local police under India's Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act, which lays down penalties for prostitution.
"She is not selling herself," Brar said. "She is only proposing to enter into a contract with a childless couple to bear them a child. What is wrong with that?"
